stimulus:
"Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -

And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard -
And sore must be the storm -
That could abash the little Bird
That kept so many warm -

I've heard it in the chillest land -
And on the strangest Sea -
Yet - never - in Extremity,
It asked a crumb - of me.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Persistence after stimulus withdrawal (the song that never stops)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TNF, serum, or a stress signal) and then withdraw it. Track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy by CUT&RUN and chromatin accessibility by ATAC-seq at days to weeks afterward. If AP-1 sites stay open and bound after the signal is gone, that supports AP-1 as a memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Sensitivity to the second stimulus (the sweetest tune in the gale)
ideas.description: Give a primed and a naive population the same second challenge. Measure the transcriptional response by RNA-seq and nascent-RNA assays, and compare the kinetics and magnitude of induction at AP-1-marked genes. Faster or stronger induction that depends on AP-1 would be the functional signature of memory.

ideas.title: Necessity and sufficiency by acute perturbation
ideas.description: Use a dominant-negative AP-1 (A-FOS), degron-tagged JUN/FOS, or CRISPRi of specific enhancers. Apply it either during priming or only during the memory (maintenance) phase, then test whether the memory response is lost. Compare with ectopic AP-1 expression alone to see if it can write memory without the original signal. Separating the establishment and maintenance phases shows whether AP-1 is needed continuously or only to start the memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell tracking of AP-1 activity and heritability
ideas.description: Use live-cell AP-1 reporters or FOS/JUN imaging, combined with lineage tracing or single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) of sister cells. Test whether the primed state is bistable, is inherited across divisions, and decays with a measurable half-life. Heritability and a stable, all-or-none state would distinguish memory from a simple lingering response.

ideas.title: Chromatin mechanism and the independence test
ideas.description: Test whether AP-1 maintains memory through chromatin remodeling (BAF/SWI-SNF), histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) and pioneer-like opening of closed sites. Perturb these factors after priming, and use optogenetic or inducible AP-1 pulses to ask whether a transient AP-1 input leaves a lasting epigenetic mark. Retained marks that persist when AP-1 is removed would show that the memory is carried by chromatin rather than by continuous AP-1 presence.
